59.name: Canada Goldenrod
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (herb default); AB retail as of 2026

59.notes: Critical late-season pollinator. Does NOT cause hay fever (wind-borne ragweed does). Spreads by rhizome.

279.name: Saskatoon Berry
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (shrub default); AB retail as of 2026

279.notes: Premier prairie fruit shrub. Extremely hardy. Fruit similar to blueberry. Self-fertile but better yield with cross-pollination.

292.name: Showy Milkweed
morphology: elliptic leaves about 15 cm long in opposite pairs

sourcing.notes: Estimate (herb default); AB retail as of 2026

292.notes: Monarch butterfly host plant. Large pink flower clusters. Milky sap. Critical conservation plant.

354.name: Trembling Aspen
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (tree default); AB retail as of 2026

354.notes: Most widely distributed tree in North America. Clonal colonies. Inner bark is survival food. Pioneer species.

387.name: White Spruce
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (large specimen tree); AB retail as of 2026

387.notes: Needle tea rich in vitamin C. Pitch used as wound sealant and chewing gum. Dominant boreal tree.

391.name: Wild Blue Flax
morphology: narrow linear leaves about 2.5 cm long
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (herb default); AB retail as of 2026

391.notes: Sky-blue flowers open daily and drop. Fibre plant historically. Excellent in dry meadow plantings.

439.name: Bee Balm (Wild Bergamot)
safety: Toxicity not assessed — absence of a warning is not a guarantee of safety

sourcing.notes: Estimate (herb default); AB retail as of 2026

439.notes: Also known as Wild Bergamot. Premier pollinator plant attracting bumblebees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Lavender-pink flowers bloom for 4-6 weeks in midsummer. Aromatic foliage deters many pest insects. Spreads by rhizome — good groundcover under light canopy.

American Goldfinch.name: American Goldfinch
American Goldfinch.description: Bright yellow seed-eating finch. Heavily dependent on Asteraceae seed (sunflower, thistle, goldenrod, aster).

Bumblebees.name: Bumblebees
Bumblebees.description: Large social bees critical for cold-climate pollination. Generalist foragers; particularly important on lupines, bergamot, asters, and goldenrods.
Bumblebees.status: Mixed — several Alberta bumble bees are at risk

Sweat Bees.name: Sweat Bees
Sweat Bees.description: Small to medium ground-nesting bees, often metallic green. Highly generalist on composites and other prairie flowers.

Red-belted Bumble Bee.name: Red-belted Bumble Bee
Red-belted Bumble Bee.description: Highly variable short-tongued bumble bee common in gardens and grassland.
facts: short tongue — needs open, shallow flowers

Bicoloured Sweat Bee.name: Bicoloured Sweat Bee
Bicoloured Sweat Bee.description: Metallic-green communal ground-nesting bee; generalist on open flowers.

Orange-legged Furrow Bee.name: Orange-legged Furrow Bee
Orange-legged Furrow Bee.description: Social sweat bee nesting in bare soil; generalist on composites.

Dark-eyed Junco.name: Dark-eyed Junco
Dark-eyed Junco.description: Ground-feeding sparrow of forest edges; winters on fallen weed seeds.

Goldenrod Soldier Beetle.name: Goldenrod Soldier Beetle
Goldenrod Soldier Beetle.description: Pollen- and nectar-feeding beetle of late-summer goldenrod; larvae are soil predators.

Drone Fly.name: Drone Fly
Drone Fly.description: Honey-bee-mimicking hover fly (introduced from Europe, now widespread); adults are major generalist pollinators of composites and umbels.

Isabella Tiger Moth.name: Isabella Tiger Moth
Isabella Tiger Moth.description: The 'woolly bear' caterpillar; a generalist on asters, goldenrods and many forbs that overwinters as a larva.
facts: A wide range of low herbaceous plants.

Northern Crescent.name: Northern Crescent
Northern Crescent.description: Small orange-and-black butterfly; caterpillars host on native asters.

Monarch.name: Monarch
Monarch.description: Iconic migratory butterfly. Caterpillars feed only on milkweeds (Asclepias). Listed as Endangered under SARA in Canada.
Monarch.status: At Risk (COSEWIC Endangered); a rare breeding migrant in Alberta
Monarch.range_notes: Migrates through southern Alberta; breeds where milkweeds occur.

Painted Lady.name: Painted Lady
Painted Lady.description: Cosmopolitan migrant butterfly. Caterpillars are generalists on Asteraceae, especially thistles.
Painted Lady.range_notes: Periodic immigrant; major irruptions every several years.

Red Admiral.name: Red Admiral
Red Admiral.description: Dark butterfly with red wing-bands. Caterpillars feed on stinging nettle.

Mormon Fritillary.name: Mormon Fritillary
Mormon Fritillary.description: Smaller orange fritillary of higher elevations. Caterpillars feed only on violets.

Milbert's Tortoiseshell.name: Milbert's Tortoiseshell
Milbert's Tortoiseshell.description: Orange-banded tortoiseshell butterfly. Caterpillars feed exclusively on stinging nettle (Urtica).
Milbert's Tortoiseshell.range_notes: Common in moist meadows and disturbed ground.

Clouded Sulphur.name: Clouded Sulphur
Clouded Sulphur.description: Ubiquitous yellow butterfly; caterpillars host on legumes (vetch, milkvetch, lupine).

Common Branded Skipper.name: Common Branded Skipper
Common Branded Skipper.description: Orange-and-brown skipper. Caterpillars feed on native bunchgrasses.

Melissa Blue.name: Melissa Blue
Melissa Blue.description: Prairie blue whose caterpillars feed on legumes and are tended by ants.

Polyphemus Moth.name: Polyphemus Moth
Polyphemus Moth.description: Large silk moth with eye-spots on hind wings. Caterpillars feed on birch, aspen, willow, and cherry.
facts: Birch, poplar, willow, chokecherry, maple and other broadleaf trees.
does not feed as an adult

Cedar Waxwing.name: Cedar Waxwing
Cedar Waxwing.description: Sleek crested songbird that feeds primarily on fruit. Strongly associated with serviceberry, mountain ash, and viburnum.
Cedar Waxwing.range_notes: Widespread breeder; nomadic in winter following fruit.

American Robin.name: American Robin
American Robin.description: Familiar thrush. Eats earthworms in spring/summer; switches to fruit (serviceberry, mountain ash, chokecherry, hawthorn) in fall and winter.

Mason Bees.name: Mason Bees
Mason Bees.description: Solitary bees that nest in cavities (bee hotels). Important pollinators of fruit trees and shrubs.
facts: nests in cavities (bee hotels, hollow stems)

Blue Orchard Mason Bee.name: Blue Orchard Mason Bee
Blue Orchard Mason Bee.description: Spring solitary bee; superb fruit-tree and willow pollinator that nests in cavities (and bee hotels).
facts: nests in cavities (bee hotels, hollow stems)

Bohemian Waxwing.name: Bohemian Waxwing
Bohemian Waxwing.description: Winter-flocking frugivore that strips berries from saskatoon, highbush-cranberry, hawthorn and rose.

Pine Grosbeak.name: Pine Grosbeak
Pine Grosbeak.description: Large winter finch that feeds on mountain-ash and other persistent fruit plus conifer and birch seeds.

Ruffed Grouse.name: Ruffed Grouse
Ruffed Grouse.description: Aspen-woodland grouse that eats poplar/willow buds, catkins and shrub fruit; broods need insect-rich understory.

Hunt's Bumble Bee.name: Hunt's Bumble Bee
Hunt's Bumble Bee.description: Common prairie/parkland bumble bee; long colony season makes it a key generalist pollinator of asters, clovers and mints.

Canadian Tiger Swallowtail.name: Canadian Tiger Swallowtail
Canadian Tiger Swallowtail.description: Large yellow-and-black swallowtail. Caterpillars feed on aspen, birch, willow, and chokecherry.
facts: Poplar, birch, willow, chokecherry and other broadleaf trees/shrubs.
Canadian Tiger Swallowtail.range_notes: Widespread across boreal and aspen parkland Alberta.

Western Tiger Swallowtail.name: Western Tiger Swallowtail
Western Tiger Swallowtail.description: Closely related to the Canadian Tiger Swallowtail. Caterpillars feed on willow, cottonwood, and chokecherry.
facts: Willow, poplar and other riparian broadleaf trees.
Western Tiger Swallowtail.range_notes: Southwestern Alberta foothills and river valleys.

Mourning Cloak.name: Mourning Cloak
Mourning Cloak.description: Dark butterfly with yellow wing borders; one of the first to emerge in spring. Caterpillars feed on willow, poplar, birch, and elm.
facts: Willow, poplar, birch and elm foliage.
Mourning Cloak.range_notes: Common throughout Alberta wherever willows occur.

Compton Tortoiseshell.name: Compton Tortoiseshell
Compton Tortoiseshell.description: Mottled brown-and-orange tortoiseshell. Caterpillars feed on birch, aspen, and willow.

White Admiral.name: White Admiral
White Admiral.description: Black butterfly with broad white wing-bands. Caterpillars feed on aspen, willow, and birch.

Black-capped Chickadee.name: Black-capped Chickadee
Black-capped Chickadee.description: Insectivorous songbird; nestlings depend almost entirely on caterpillars. Native trees rich in lepidoptera (aspen, willow, birch, cherry) anchor its food supply.

Great Horned Owl.name: Great Horned Owl
Great Horned Owl.description: Alberta's provincial bird; nests in poplar/spruce, controls rodents.

Northern Flicker.name: Northern Flicker
Northern Flicker.description: Ground-foraging woodpecker that eats ants and autumn fruit; nests in aspen/poplar snags.

Downy Woodpecker.name: Downy Woodpecker
Downy Woodpecker.description: Smallest woodpecker; forages insects on shrubs and trees and excavates nest cavities in soft dead wood (poplar, birch).

Silver-haired Bat.name: Silver-haired Bat
Silver-haired Bat.description: Migratory tree bat roosting under bark of poplar and spruce.

Big Poplar Sphinx.name: Big Poplar Sphinx
Big Poplar Sphinx.description: Large hawkmoth whose caterpillars feed on poplar and willow foliage.
facts: does not feed as an adult

Spotted Tussock Moth.name: Spotted Tussock Moth
Spotted Tussock Moth.description: Tussock caterpillar feeding on willow, poplar, alder and birch.
facts: Poplar, willow, birch, alder and maple.
does not feed as an adult

Red-breasted Nuthatch.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
Red-breasted Nuthatch.description: Conifer specialist that eats spruce/pine seeds and bark insects; nests in cavities.

Merlin.name: Merlin
Merlin.description: Small falcon that reuses old crow/magpie nests in spruce; hunts small birds in towns and parkland.

Canada Jay.name: Canada Jay
Canada Jay.description: Boreal/foothills jay that caches food in spruce; year-round resident.

Small Sweat Bees.name: Small Sweat Bees
Small Sweat Bees.description: Hugely diverse genus of tiny ground-nesting generalist pollinators — among the most abundant bees in any Alberta garden.

White-lined Sphinx.name: White-lined Sphinx
White-lined Sphinx.description: Day-and-dusk hawkmoth; a hummingbird-like nectar pollinator of tubular flowers; larvae feed on flax and evening-primrose family plants.
facts: Fireweed, evening-primrose, purslane and many herbs.
